properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.bridge-error-handler
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.configuration
properties.description: The configuration that each endpoint of this component starts from. The options of the endpoint URI override its values. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.google.firestore.GoogleFirestoreConfiguration type.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.database-id
properties.description: The Firestore database ID. If not specified, the default database '(default)' will be used.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.document-id
properties.description: The ID of the document for setDocument, getDocumentById, updateDocument and deleteDocument, which fail without one. For listCollections it is the document whose subcollections are listed, and if not set the root collections are listed. The CamelGoogleFirestoreDocumentId header replaces this option.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the google-firestore component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.firestore-client
properties.description: To use a custom com.google.cloud.firestore.Firestore client. When this option is set or autowired, the projectId, databaseId and serviceAccountKey options are not used. The Camel endpoint does not close a client that is set or autowired. The option is a com.google.cloud.firestore.Firestore type.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.health-check-consumer-enabled
properties.description: Used for enabling or disabling all consumer based health checks from this component

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.health-check-producer-enabled
properties.description: Used for enabling or disabling all producer based health checks from this component. Notice: Camel has by default disabled all producer based health-checks. You can turn on producer checks globally by setting camel.health.producersEnabled=true.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.max-pending-changes
properties.description: Maximum number of realtime document changes buffered between two polls. The changes reported by the snapshot listener are buffered until the next poll picks them up, so a collection changing faster than the route consumes it makes that buffer grow. When the buffer is full the oldest buffered change is discarded and a warning is logged. Use 0 for an unbounded buffer. Only used when realtimeUpdates is enabled.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.operation
properties.description: The operation that the producer performs. If not set, the producer performs setDocument. The CamelGoogleFirestoreOperation header replaces this option.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.project-id
properties.description: The ID of the Google Cloud project. If not set, the Firestore client takes it from the service account key, or from the environment, such as the GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT environment variable.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.realtime-updates
properties.description: Whether the consumer listens for realtime changes of the collection with a snapshot listener. The first snapshot reports every existing document as ADDED, and each poll routes the changes buffered since the previous poll. If false, each poll reads all documents of the collection, so a document is consumed again in every poll.

properties.name: camel.component.google-firestore.service-account-key
properties.description: The service account key file in JSON format that the Firestore client uses as credentials. It is loaded from the classpath by default, or from another location with the prefix file: or http:. If not set, the client uses Application Default Credentials.
